scored.stack: WinUI 3 / Windows App SDK 2.0 (C#/.NET 10, WinRT, Microsoft.UI.Composition, Microsoft.UI.Xaml, Win2D + ComputeSharp.D2D1.WinUI, Win32 P/Invoke for ConPTY, Job Objects and window-style interop), unpackaged + self-contained, NSIS/MSI installer.
scored.verdict: VIABLE - the earlier DISQUALIFIED verdict is overturned, because it rested entirely on the desktop-sampling bridge that OD-0005 has now removed, and Windows App SDK 2.0's new SystemBackdropElement additionally destroys the "one window-wide material enum" objection; but it re-enters as a mid-field candidate, not a front-runner, because a custom fragment shader on this stack can only read images the app owns through Direct2D, and XAML-rendered content is not one of them, so glass half (b) is only fully reachable over content the port renders itself in Win2D.

scored.stack: Avalonia UI 12.1.2 on .NET 10 (C#), rendering through SkiaSharp 3.119.4 / Skia with HarfBuzzSharp 8.3.1.3 shaping, the Avalonia composition renderer, and Win32/WinRT interop via Avalonia.Controls.Platform.Win32Properties plus ordinary P/Invoke. Terminal via ConPTY (Devolutions.Terminal.Control, or hand-rolled). Packaging and update via Velopack.
scored.verdict: VIABLE. With OD-0005 removing the desktop-sampling requirement, the one thing Avalonia could not do is no longer asked for, and the stack now satisfies both halves of the glass requirement with first-party APIs and clears the other eleven constraints with no fatal gap, at the price of three named platform ceilings (lock-state secrets, non-activating-panel semantics, DWM window animations under custom chrome) and one large but predictable re-expression cost.

scored.stack: Native Win32 + Direct3D 11 + Direct2D/DirectWrite + DirectComposition (C++20), HLSL for the 22 per-site materials and the Genie distortion, ConPTY + Job Objects for process supervision, DwmSetWindowAttribute(DWMWA_SYSTEMBACKDROP_TYPE, DWMSBT_TRANSIENTWINDOW) or Windows App SDK DesktopAcrylicController for the desktop-facing acrylic. Windows.Graphics.Capture is DROPPED from this stack definition per OD-0005.
scored.verdict: VIABLE - and the verdict materially improves, because the adversary pass that returned BREAKS returned it almost entirely on the Windows.Graphics.Capture path that OD-0005 has now deleted; but the stack no longer holds any capability the field cannot match, so it must now win on cost alone, and on cost it is the most expensive of the eight.

scored.stack: Electron 44.4.1 (Chromium 152 + Node), TypeScript; node-pty 1.1.0 (ConPTY) + xterm.js; @parcel/watcher 2.6.0 for filesystem watch; electron-builder/electron-updater (NSIS) with a hand-rolled GitLab Releases check; one small native helper (or prebuilt addon) for Job Objects.
scored.verdict: VIABLE - the removal of desktop sampling deletes the one thing Electron structurally could not do, and both glass halves are now reachable through documented, verified mechanisms, one of which is already running in the owner's own Electron 44 build; what remains is a large but bounded semantic-translation bill (constraint 11) plus two named native-behaviour deviations (Snap Layouts flyout, Job Object group kill).

decision.recommendation: Avalonia UI 12.1.2 on .NET 10 (C#), rendering through SkiaSharp 3.119.4 with HarfBuzzSharp 8.3.1.3 shaping and the Avalonia composition renderer; glass as an app-owned two-pass compositor driving SKSL runtime effects (SKRuntimeEffect / SKRuntimeEffectUniforms / SKRuntimeEffectChildren) through ISkiaSharpApiLeaseFeature; acrylic edge via Window.TransparencyLevelHint = WindowTransparencyLevel.AcrylicBlur per window; Win32 interop by P/Invoke plus Win32Properties (AddWindowStylesCallback, AddWndProcHookCallback, SetNonClientHitTestResult); ConPTY + Job Objects in one PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE list via hand-rolled CreateProcessW; packaging and update via Velopack with a hand-written GitLab Releases check.
decision.runner_up: WinUI 3 / Windows App SDK (C#/.NET 10, Microsoft.UI.Xaml, SystemBackdropElement + AcrylicBrush, Win2D / ComputeSharp.D2D1.WinUI for shaders, Win32 P/Invoke for ConPTY, Job Objects and window interop), unpackaged and self-contained.
decision.why:
The four contenders all clear glass (a) and all clear constraints 4-7 and 10 with comparable Win32 interop. They separate on two things: glass (b) over live content, and semantic translation cost.

On glass (b) I did not take either scorecard's word for where the 22 sites sit. Grepping the spec records for glassEffect shows them predominantly over live app-rendered content, not over a static wallpaper layer: TimelineMinimap.swift:306-344 previewCard over the transcript; ComposerView.swift:1293-1307 ComposerSurface over the chat; CommandPalette.swift:96-98 over the whole window; RequestCards.swift:62-64, FollowUpQueueTab.swift:150-155, ThreadChangesTab.swift:36-44 in the composer flow; FloatingSidebarPanel.swift:87-102 and UsageFloatingPanel.swift:53-63 over panes; EffortSlider.swift:781-796 over an app-drawn track. WinUI 3's own scorecard concedes a D2D pixel shader cannot read XAML-composed pixels and that PixelShaderEffect carries [NoComposition]. Given where the sites actually are, full material on WinUI 3 means re-rendering the transcript, composer and panes in immediate-mode Win2D: discarding the framework exactly where a framework earns its keep (text editing, IME, accessibility, virtualised lists) while still paying the XAML dependency. That is a structural fork of unbounded blast radius. Avalonia already renders everything through Skia, so one explicit two-pass compositor covers all 22 sites uniformly, with no fork. Separately, .interactive() appears at Chrome.swift:178, the EffortSlider knob and ThreadChangesTab; AcrylicBrush has no pointer-tracked deformation, so those become flat approximations - a visible product deviation, which the brief ranks worse than developer effort. Avalonia also draws true .continuous squircle corners in the shader; WinUI 3's CornerRadius is a circular arc at every one of the 22 radii.

Three facts I verified here, correcting both scorecards: .NET SDK 10.0.401 is already installed (dotnet --list-sdks), so Avalonia needs zero toolchain installs; Avalonia.Skia 12.1.2's nuspec declares a net10.0 dependency group pinning SkiaSharp 3.119.4 and HarfBuzzSharp 8.3.1.3 (the original eval's 4.152.x was wrong, and WinAppSDK's net10.0-windows support remains an unresolved probe); and symbol inspection of the shipped net10.0 assemblies confirms ISkiaSharpApiLeaseFeature, ISkiaSharpApiLease, SkSurface, SkCanvas, GrContext in Avalonia.Skia.dll and SKRuntimeEffect, SKRuntimeEffectUniforms, SKRuntimeEffectChildren, SKRuntimeShaderBuilder, SKRoundRect in SkiaSharp.dll.

On constraint 11 Avalonia is joint-best: one process, one UI thread, Dispatcher.UIThread plus AvaloniaSynchronizationContext carry the 256 @MainActor annotations and the sessionEpoch / finishingTurnID / unsentSessionID ordering rules as written. It also clears constraint 5's ordering problem by construction (PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST beside PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PSEUDOCONSOLE in one attribute list), which Electron needs a native helper for.
decision.why_not_runner_up: WinUI 3 is the right runner-up and would become the pick if probe P1 fails, because then neither stack can shader over live content and WinUI 3's cleaner packaging story and stronger OverlappedPresenter window API decide it. It loses on one structural fact: Win2D/ComputeSharp PixelShaderEffect can only consume images the app owns through Direct2D, and XAML-composed pixels are not one of them. CompositionVisualSurface keeps its result inside composition; RenderTargetBitmap is an async one-shot, not a per-frame source. Because the spec shows most of the 22 sites over live app content, the full material is reachable only by re-expressing the transcript, composer and panes as immediate-mode Win2D drawing - the framework's controls, text editing, IME and accessibility surrendered for the subtrees rewritten, with the XAML dependency retained. Avalonia pays no such fork. Secondary: .interactive() deformation is unreachable on AcrylicBrush; CornerRadius is a circular arc rather than a .continuous squircle at all 22 radii; live-resize is a documented longstanding weakness with multiple open issues (microsoft-ui-xaml #2506, #5148, #10820, #10374) rather than merely unverified; and whether SystemBackdropElement + DesktopAcrylicBackdrop nested inside a window shows the desktop or only app content is unsettled by the docs, while net10.0-windows support is unstated in the release notes the evaluator fetched - I checked the Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK 2.5.1 nuspec and it is a metapackage with no lib folders, so it does not settle it either.
disqualified: Native Win32 + Direct3D 11 + Direct2D/DirectWrite + DirectComposition (C++20) - not disqualified on capability; rejected on cost with no remaining capability advantage. Under OD-0005 its unique card (desktop pixels as a shadable texture) is no longer required, and glass (b) over app-drawn content is matched by Avalonia. It then fails constraint 11 outright: C++ has no @MainActor enforcement, so 256 call sites are hand-audited against a hand-built dispatcher with the failure mode a data race rather than a build error; plus a hand-built control set for 1029 UI contract records, a hand-written UI Automation provider tree (Microsoft documents this as non-optional for custom controls), TSF ITextStoreACP for IME, and a terminal emulator with no SwiftTerm equivalent to port from. Its own scorecard estimates 2.5-4x the engineering, concentrated in work with the least parity leverage. It also needs MSVC v143 plus cmake (7-10 GB), neither installed, against a brief requiring probes runnable with what is on this machine.

Electron 44.4.1 - viable and cheapest to start, ranked third. Its glass mechanism is genuinely proven in the owner's own Electron 44 build (src/renderer/components/glass.tsx), and its packaging/update objections were overturned (builder-util-runtime does ship a gitlab PublishProvider). It loses on constraint 11, which is the contract's own tiebreak: a main process plus roughly a dozen renderer processes reached by asynchronous IPC and structured clone, across 192 Swift files and 86,076 lines, with every §5.6 ordering invariant rebuilt by hand across a process boundary that Swift's main-actor confinement made impossible to violate. That is the single largest and least reversible semantic translation in the field, and it produces correctness bugs rather than cosmetic ones. Secondary: no WM_NCHITTEST hook at all (electron#31372 closed without one), so Snap Layouts are lost outright; focusable:false forces skipTaskbar and blocks keyboard input, so the MCP secret panels cannot use it; and backdrop-filter:url() has no second implementation (WebKit bug 245510, w3c/svgwg#1142), making the Chromium pin load-bearing for the product's visual identity. Also weigh the adversary's circularity finding: the derived corpus already names Electron 16+ times in windows_path fields, so corpus support for Electron is partly self-referential.

Tauri 2 (Rust + WebView2) - was disqualified on desktop sampling, which OD-0005 removes, but it was not re-scored and does not win if it were: it inherits every Electron semantic-translation cost with a smaller and less proven Windows window-control surface, needs MSVC plus rustup (8-12 GB, neither installed), and window-vibrancy gives a window-wide material, not 22 per-site ones.

Flutter 3.47.2 - same: the disqualifier (no API hands a Flutter window the desktop as a texture) is vacated, and Impeller can author the full material over Flutter-painted content. It still loses on multi-window maturity against contract section 10's 'do not reduce multiple panels to one page', on a Dart runtime that re-expresses rather than transliterates the Core and Services layers, and on needing MSVC + CMake (9-15 GB, not installed).

WPF (.NET 10, MILCore) - disqualifier partly vacated, but ShaderEffect is Direct3D 9 pixel shader model 3.0 with no access to the pixels beneath a given element, and reaching a modern shader means D3DImage/HwndHost airspace interop; it is strictly worse than Avalonia at the one thing that decides this choice, with no offsetting advantage.
deviations_this_choice_forces: Avalonia's acrylic recipe is hardcoded (WinUiCompositionUtils.CreateAcrylicBlurBackdropBrush, a fixed WinUIGaussianBlurEffect plus saturation), so DesktopAcrylicController's TintColor/TintOpacity/LuminosityOpacity knobs are not exposed. The source's tint and the 0.26 dark / 0.18 light scrim must be drawn by the app as a layer over the system material. Functionally equivalent, mechanically different; record it.

The outer window corner is DWM's circular-arc DWMWA_WINDOW_CORNER_PREFERENCE (or Avalonia's CompositionRoundedRectangleGeometry clip), not a .continuous squircle. The 22 INNER sites do not inherit this deviation, because their geometry is app-drawn and a superellipse SDF in SKSL reproduces .continuous exactly - this is a point where Avalonia is strictly better than the runner-up, and the deviation is limited to the window frame.

The glass subsystem depends on ISkiaSharpApiLeaseFeature / ISkiaSharpApiLease, which are attributed [Unstable] and carry no cross-minor compatibility promise. The port must pin its Avalonia version and gate every upgrade behind a screenshot regression suite. Record this as a maintenance deviation, not a capability one.

AvaloniaUI/Avalonia#21212: in v12, WindowDecorations='BorderOnly' plus ExtendClientAreaToDecorationsHint strips WS_CAPTION/WS_MINIMIZEBOX/WS_MAXIMIZEBOX, which DWM needs for minimize/maximize/restore animations and for Snap Layouts, while 'Full' preserves them but draws OS caption glyphs over the app's controls. The source has neither Windows animations nor Snap Layouts, so losing them is the parity-correct trade, but it is a departure from Windows convention and P7 must record which value is chosen and what it costs.

AppKit shapes the window shadow to the window's alpha so it follows the rounded card. DWM does not do this for a WS_EX_NOREDIRECTIONBITMAP window, so the shadow is app-drawn inside the window with reserved transparent margins at all four chromeless surfaces, and every frame and hit-test constant shifts accordingly.

Skia is not CoreText. Glyph rasterisation, hinting and subpixel behaviour will differ (mono/SkiaSharp#2308). Under OD-0001 this is already UNVERIFIABLE for every candidate, so it costs nothing relative to the field, but it is a named deviation on this stack as on any.
Neither .NET nor Avalonia ships an audio API, so ToneSynth / FinishChime / SettleChime need NAudio over WASAPI or direct XAudio2 P/Invoke. An added dependency, not a behaviour change.

Platform ceilings identical across all four contenders, listed for completeness rather than as discriminators: NSPanel [.nonactivatingPanel] semantics (Windows has no app-active/window-key split; the recommendation is to let the two MCP secret panels activate and record it); kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked (DPAPI CurrentUser and Credential Manager both stay available while the workstation is locked); NSWindow.collectionBehavior .canJoinAllSpaces (no public pin-to-all-virtual-desktops API); acrylic flattening to a solid FallbackColor under Transparency-effects-off, Battery Saver, low-end hardware and High Contrast, which is OS policy and outside the app's control; and Chrome.trafficLightTop / trafficLightDiameter having no Windows analogue to re-derive from.
biggest_risks: P1 fails: the app-owned two-pass glass compositor does not work cleanly, or ISkiaSharpApiLease.SkSurface is null in a CompositionCustomVisualHandler render. This is the whole basis of choosing Avalonia over WinUI 3. Mitigation: fall back to ICustomDrawOperation and re-run P1; if that also fails, Avalonia's advantage over the runner-up evaporates entirely and the decision reopens in favour of WinUI 3, which is why P1 is first and why no production code is written before it passes. Do NOT build on lease.SkSurface.Snapshot() ambiently - AvaloniaUI/Avalonia#16985 documents it leaving blank spots where child controls sit and glitching on hover and click, with a maintainer declining to endorse it; own the pass structure instead.

Live resize (P4) is the least-verified constraint on this stack. Avalonia's Win32 backend handles WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE/WM_EXITSIZEMOVE only to flip _resizeReason (WindowImpl.AppWndProc.cs:712, :776); it installs no timer to keep UI-thread animation ticking inside Windows' modal size/move loop, and WindowImpl.cs:1183 carries a maintainer comment about margin artefacts when resizing with extended client area under WinUI composition (issue #8316). Acrylic plus extended client area plus a live shader surface plus a running spring is the worst case, on an AMD integrated GPU. Mitigation: probe before signing; if it fails, ship reduced-fidelity glass during resize as a named deviation, and decide it BEFORE the chrome is designed because it changes the design. Note this is not a reason to prefer WinUI 3, where the same weakness is worse documented (microsoft-ui-xaml #2506, #5148, #10820).

Schedule, not capability: re-expressing 1029 UI contract records as XAML plus Panel/Layoutable subclasses with MeasureOverride/ArrangeOverride is the bulk of the work and the most likely way the port misses a date even when every hard constraint holds. Mitigation: in week one, triage all 22 glass sites and the full UI contract into two-pass-glass surfaces versus plain surfaces, build the glass compositor first against the tour-*@2x.png oracle (with OD-0004's approximate-oracle caveat attached), and only then start the bulk of the views - so the irreversible architectural decision is made against real pixels rather than in the abstract.

Snapshot cost at real scale (P2). Every snapshot is a GPU texture copy; Chrome.swift:219 already records that a window-sized glass surface is a full-window backdrop sample every frame on hardware far better than this target. Mitigation: three shared snapshots per frame using the GlassEffectContainer spacing groups (2, 2, 8) rather than 22; if that still misses budget, glass over the live transcript specifically must be cached and invalidated on content change, which costs fidelity exactly where it is most visible - record it rather than tuning it silently.

The glass subsystem sits on an [Unstable] API. Mitigation: pin the Avalonia version in Directory.Packages.props, build P10's regression harness before production code, and treat any Avalonia bump as a visual change requiring re-approval.

UNK-0023 is now the highest-value open question and should be resolved early: if the app always draws its own backdrop, every one of the 22 sites gets the full shader material and the acrylic becomes purely the edge the owner named. If it does not, sites over a bare transparent window degrade to tint-over-acrylic with no lensing. This is a product decision that changes how much of glass (b) is actually reachable, and it should go to the owner before the compositor is designed.
probes_before_committing: P1 - THE DECIDING PROBE. Two-pass glass over live app content. Build one Avalonia 12.1.2 net10.0 window: an app-drawn opaque wallpaper base, a simulated scrolling transcript with high-contrast text beneath, and a rounded-rect CompositionCustomVisual whose handler renders the backdrop subtree into an APP-OWNED offscreen SKSurface (not lease.SkSurface.Snapshot of the ambient surface), then runs an SKRuntimeEffect over it as a uniform shader child with edge-concentrated displacement, per-channel RGB sample offsets, a luminance-derived specular rim, a .continuous superellipse SDF mask, and a pointer-position uniform driven by RegisterForNextAnimationFrameUpdate / OnAnimationFrameUpdate. PASS: the rim tracks the pointer at input rate; chromatic fringing is visible where the shape crosses high-contrast transcript text; and screenshots taken while scrolling AND while hovering a child control show NO blank regions (the #16985 failure mode). FAIL on any of the three: retry via ICustomDrawOperation; if it still fails, reopen the stack decision in favour of WinUI 3. Runnable today: dotnet SDK 10.0.401 is installed, Avalonia 12.1.2 declares a net10.0 group, and I confirmed ISkiaSharpApiLeaseFeature/ISkiaSharpApiLease/SkSurface/SkCanvas/GrContext in Avalonia.Skia.dll and SKRuntimeEffect/SKRuntimeEffectUniforms/SKRuntimeEffectChildren/SKRuntimeShaderBuilder/SKRoundRect in SkiaSharp.dll, both net10.0, by symbol inspection of the shipped packages.

P2 - Snapshot budget at production scale. Instrument P1's scene scaled to the real count: 22 glass sites grouped into 3 shared-snapshot groups (GlassEffectContainer spacings 2, 2, 8), window 1320x860, over a transcript streaming at the source's 45 ms flush cadence with .interactive() pointer tracking live. PASS: median frame time <= 16.7 ms and 99th percentile <= 33 ms on this AMD integrated GPU, measured by an in-app frame timer with GPU time for the snapshot pass reported separately and staying under about 3 ms. FAIL: glass over the live transcript must be cached and invalidated on content change - record the fidelity cost before committing.

P3 - Acrylic edge over the desktop, and the layered-window trap. Set Window.TransparencyLevelHint = WindowTransparencyLevel.AcrylicBlur on an Avalonia 12 window with ExtendClientAreaToDecorationsHint true, over a high-contrast desktop wallpaper, and capture with Alt+PrtScn so the window KEEPS FOCUS (background acrylic is documented to flatten to a solid colour on deactivation; pin SystemBackdropConfiguration-equivalent behaviour rather than tracking activation). PASS: desktop content is visibly blurred and tinted through the window, AND the capture's sha256 differs from a bare desktop grab. This is the exact abort condition the repository's own E:/Droppy/port/porting/probes/acrylic_window.ps1 already hit - control_solid.png, desktop_plain.png, acrylic_real.png and acrylic_excluded_from_capture.png are all sha256 98d72e76..., four byte-identical desktop grabs, because Form.TransparencyKey set WS_EX_LAYERED and DWM system backdrops do not apply to layered windows. Assert in the probe that the Avalonia window is never WS_EX_LAYERED. FAIL: fall back to a DwmSetWindowAttribute(DWMWA_SYSTEMBACKDROP_TYPE, DWMSBT_TRANSIENTWINDOW) P/Invoke on TopLevel.TryGetPlatformHandle().Handle, and if that shows nothing, force Win32CompositionMode.RedirectionSurface for that window and re-probe.

P4 - Acrylic plus extended client area plus live resize, all three at once. Drag-resize a 1320x860 frameless acrylic window running P1's glass surface and a spring animation. PASS: no margin artefact at any edge (WindowImpl.cs:1183 / issue #8316), and the spring shows no visible stall, snap or discontinuity across WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE and WM_EXITSIZEMOVE, with per-frame times logged. FAIL: record 'animation not held during live resize' as a named deviation and decide the reduced-fidelity resize behaviour BEFORE the chrome is designed.

P5 - ConPTY and Job Object in ONE attribute list, from C# P/Invoke. InitializeProcThreadAttributeList with dwAttributeCount 2; UpdateProcThreadAttribute with PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PSEUDOCONSOLE and PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST; CreateProcessW with EXTENDED_STARTUPINFO_PRESENT and a blittable STARTUPINFOEXW; one servicing thread per channel per Microsoft's deadlock warning. Launch claude.exe with a harmless non-model argument only (--version or --help): no prompt, no sign-in, no credential file read, per the repository's safety rules. PASS: pty output arrives on both channels; ResizePseudoConsole changes the child's reported column count; and TerminateJobObject kills both the child AND a grandchild it spawned, with no CREATE_SUSPENDED / ResumeThread race anywhere in the path. FAIL: the whole process-supervision design changes and must be redesigned before the supervisor is written.

P6 - Graceful-then-forceful termination with the one-second gap, per transport. Three cases against scripted fixture stand-ins (never a signed-in agent): 0x03 written into ConPTY input for a pty child; stdin close then CTRL_BREAK via an AttachConsole / GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent(CTRL_BREAK_EVENT) / FreeConsole helper for a CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP console child; and TerminateJobObject at the deadline. PASS: a cooperating fixture exits before t+1000 ms and a deliberately non-cooperating one is terminated at t+1000 ms, both timestamps logged within +/- 50 ms, and a write to a closed pipe surfaces as IOException with ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE or ERROR_NO_DATA and is handled as recoverable. This reproduces C4 / Shell.swift:110-118 / StdioProcess.swift:114-120 rather than collapsing the pair into one kill.

P7 - Chrome and windowing, four things in one window. ExtendClientAreaToDecorationsHint plus ExtendClientAreaTitleBarHeightHint plus WindowDecorations; app-drawn caption buttons on the LEADING edge at the derived traffic-light constants (titlebarHeight 44, 14 px buttons on a 23 px pitch, leading 18/14, top 16/21); Win32Properties.SetNonClientHitTestResult declaring those controls Caption / Close / MinButton / MaxButton; and, in the same run, a second window carrying WS_EX_NOACTIVATE (via Win32Properties.AddWindowStylesCallback) with a WM_MOUSEACTIVATE / MA_NOACTIVATE hook (AddWndProcHookCallback) containing a password field. PASS: drag, double-click-to-maximise and the system context menu all work from the app-drawn region; the app-drawn buttons minimise, maximise and close; AND the user can type into the non-activating panel's field. The probe MUST also record, for each WindowDecorations value, whether the Snap Layouts hover flyout appears over the leading-edge maximise button and whether DWM minimize/maximize/restore animations survive - this is AvaloniaUI/Avalonia#21212 and the answer fixes the chrome deviation list before any of it is designed.

P8 - Filesystem watch overflow signal. Point a System.IO.FileSystemWatcher with InternalBufferSize at its 4 KB minimum at a repo-shaped tree and generate a burst (a git checkout across a large branch, or a scripted 10,000-file touch). PASS: the Error event fires carrying InternalBufferOverflowException at least once, and the app's full-rescan path runs to completion. This is the 'we lost events, rescan' semantic that C6's three FSEvents loss flags require. FAIL: move to ReadDirectoryChangesW with overlapped I/O by P/Invoke and re-probe for ERROR_NOTIFY_ENUM_DIR and for the documented zero-lpBytesReturned overflow.

P9 - Text metrics that feed layout. Using Avalonia.Media.TextFormatting (TextLayout, TextFormatter, TextShaper, ShapedTextRun, TextLineMetrics, TextBounds, TextLineBreak), implement the source's first-party type scale and measure a fixed fixture corpus. PASS: measured wrap points and line counts for the fixture strings match the visible wrap points in the tour-*@2x.png oracle at the recorded sizes, and the 50 monospaced sites hold column alignment under Cascadia Mono with tabular figures. This probe validates MEASUREMENT only; glyph rasterisation stays UNVERIFIED under OD-0001 and the OD-0004 approximate-oracle caveat travels with every number taken from the PNGs.

P10 - Regression harness for the [Unstable] lease API, built BEFORE production code. Capture reference screenshots of P1's scene, then bump Avalonia to the next available patch and re-run. PASS: output is byte-comparable, or every difference is explainable and approved. Without this harness the glass subsystem has no upgrade path, because ISkiaSharpApiLeaseFeature carries no cross-minor compatibility promise.

P11 - Packaging and update smoke test. dotnet publish -r win-x64 self-contained; dotnet tool install -g vpk and vpk pack; then a single unauthenticated GET to the public GitLab Releases API with an all-or-nothing lenient six-field decode. PASS: the installer installs and launches on this machine as an ordinary desktop app with no dev server, no WSL and no browser tab; and the check emits PR-UPDATE-019/020/027's literal strings byte-for-byte on both the success and the unreachable paths, including the U+2019 apostrophe in "Couldn't reach GitLab.". Installer signature verification is written against WinVerifyTrust / X509Certificate2 but stays untestable end to end until UNK-0009 (no Windows release asset, no certificate) is closed - that is a project gap, not a stack gap. Every step here runs with the .NET SDK 10.0.401 already installed; no MSVC, no cmake, no Rust.
